english: In the time of the lawless champions of idolatry, impious orders against the Christians practicing true worship were posted in every city and countryside. They compelled them to pour a drink-offering to the vain idols.
After their arrest, the holy men were brought before Rusticus, the prefect of Rome.
title: Impious orders and arrest

orientation: The narrator opens the account as orders go out against the Christians and the holy men are arrested and brought to Rusticus the prefect of Rome.

english: Once they stood before his tribunal, Rusticus the prefect said to Justin, "First obey the gods and obey the emperors." Justin answered, "It is blameless and beyond condemnation to obey what our Savior Jesus Christ commanded."

The prefect asked, "What teachings do you handle?" Justin answered, "I have tried to learn every teaching, but I have given my assent to the true teachings, those of the Christians, even when they displease people of false opinions." Rusticus the prefect said, "Do those teachings please you, you utter wretch?" Justin answered, "Yes, for I follow them with right teaching." The prefect asked, "What is that teaching?"

Justin answered, "It is that we give true worship to the God of the Christians. We hold him to be the one God from the beginning, the maker and fashioner of all creation, visible and invisible. And we hold the Lord Jesus Christ to be the servant of God. He was proclaimed beforehand by the prophets as the one who would come to the human race as a herald of salvation and a teacher of good lessons. I am only human, so whatever I say is small beside his boundless divinity, and I confess I speak only with a share of prophetic power. For he whom I just called the Son of God was proclaimed beforehand, and the prophets long ago foretold his coming among humans."
title: Obeying Christ and stating the Christian teaching about God
translator_notes: Promoted 2026-10-19: passing Muse-lane draft (20261019T031415Z), blind-gloss critic pass, gate clean.
orientation: Justin, the Christian teacher, is now questioned before the tribunal by Rusticus the prefect who orders obedience to the gods and the emperors.

title: Where the Christians Gather
english: Rusticus the prefect asked, "Where do you meet?" Justin answered, "Wherever each person chooses and is able. You surely suppose we all gather in the same place? It is not so. The God of the Christians is not circumscribed by place. He remains unseen, yet he fills heaven and earth, and everywhere he is worshiped and glorified by believers."

Rusticus the prefect said, "Tell me, where do you meet, and in what place do you gather your learners?" Justin answered, "I lodge above the bathhouse of Martinus son of Timothinus. I have stayed there through all this time, and this is my second stay in the city of Rome. I know no other meeting except the one there. Whenever anyone wished to visit me, I shared the teachings of the truth with him."
Rusticus asked, "So you are a Christian?" Justin answered, "Yes, I am a Christian."

orientation: The prefect Rusticus questions Justin about where Christians assemble, and Justin explains that God is not confined to place and describes his lodging in Rome.

title: Each prisoner declares being Christian
english: Rusticus the prefect said to Chariton, “You as well, Chariton — tell me, are you a Christian?” Chariton said, “I am a Christian by God’s command.” Rusticus the prefect said to Charito, “What do you say, Charito?” Charito said, “I am a Christian by God’s gift.” Rusticus said to Euelpistus, “And who are you?” Euelpistus, a slave of Caesar, answered, “I too am a Christian. I was freed by Christ, and I share in the same hope by Christ’s grace.”

Rusticus the prefect said to Hierax, “Are you also a Christian?” Hierax said, “Yes, I am a Christian. I revere and worship the same God.” Rusticus the prefect said, “Did Justin make you Christians?” Hierax said, “I was a Christian, and I will be one.” Paeon, who stood by, said, “I too am a Christian.” Rusticus the prefect said, “Who taught you?” Paeon said, “We received this good confession from our parents.” Euelpistus said, “I gladly listened to Justin’s teachings, but I too received being a Christian from my parents.” Rusticus the prefect said, “Where are your parents?” Euelpistus said, “In Cappadocia.”

Rusticus said to Hierax, “Where are your parents?” He answered, “Our true father is Christ, and our mother is faith in him. My earthly parents have died. I was torn away from Iconium in Phrygia and have come here.” Rusticus the prefect said to Liberianus, “And what do you say? Are you a Christian? Do you not practice true worship either?” Liberianus said, “I too am a Christian. I practice true worship and worship the only true God.”

orientation: After Justin confesses, Rusticus the prefect questions each companion in turn about being Christian.

title: Refusing to leave true worship for impiety
english: The prefect said to Justin, “Listen, you who are called learned and claim to know the true teachings. If you are scourged and then beheaded, are you convinced that you will go up to heaven?” Justin said, “I hope to have a home there if I endure these things. For I know that the gift from God remains for all who have lived in this way until the fulfillment of the whole world.”

Rusticus the prefect said, “So you suppose that you will go up to the heavens and receive some rewards in return?” Justin said, “I do not suppose it. I know it and am fully assured of it.” Rusticus the prefect said, “Now let us turn to the pressing matter before us. Join together with one mind and offer sacrifice to the gods.” Justin said, “No one of sound mind moves from true worship into impiety.” Rusticus the prefect said, “If you do not obey, you will be punished without mercy.” Justin said, “Our prayer is to be punished for the sake of our Lord Jesus Christ and so be saved, because this will become for us salvation and boldness before the judge at the most fearful and universal judgment seat of our Master and Savior.” The other witnesses said likewise, “Do what you please. For we are Christians, and to idols we do not offer sacrifice.”

Rusticus the prefect passed sentence, saying, “Those who have refused to offer sacrifice to the gods and to yield to the emperor’s order are to be scourged and led away to pay the capital penalty by beheading, as the laws direct.”

title: Execution and burial of the witnesses
english: The holy martyrs glorified God. They went out to the usual place and were beheaded, and in the confession of the Savior they completed their witness.
Some of the faithful secretly took their bodies and laid them in a suitable place, with the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ working with them. To him be glory forever and ever, amen.
